questions.passage: I don’t remember many conversations I had in Tokyo with professors, deans, or even friends around that time. Yet many things that happened during my study abroad are still vivid in my memory. For instance, I shared my dorm room with a student named Mike. I’d often pick up the phone and hear, “Is Mike there?” and I’d say, “No.”
questions.prompt: What memory contrast introduces the dorm-room example?
options: Many study-abroad events remain vivid, unlike numerous conversations from the same period in Tokyo.
The author remembers every Tokyo conversation but nothing from abroad.
Only conversations about music are remembered from either country.
All memories of his roommate Mike have disappeared.
questions.promptZh: 宿舍例子前，作者先作了什么记忆对比？
optionsZh: 许多留学事件仍清晰，而同期在东京的许多谈话已记不清。
东京每次谈话都记得，国外一件事也不记得。
两个国家都只记得音乐谈话。
与室友 Mike 有关的记忆全部消失。
analyses: A don’t remember many 对照 still vivid，正是例子引出的对比。
B 把两地的记忆状态倒置，并扩大为每次与全无。
C 本段没有 only music，下一例是接电话。
D 作者正举出与 Mike 同住和接电话的清晰记忆。

many things that happened during my study abroad are still vivid in my memory.

questions.passage: Later, psychologists had a large pool of participants rate themselves using many of the original Allport-Odbert terms, then applied the statistical technique of factor analysis to sort the terms into larger groups, or “factors.”
questions.prompt: How did the psychologists organise the personality terms into broader factors?
options: They asked raters to choose the five most familiar words without statistical analysis.
They collected self-ratings and used factor analysis to group the terms.
They treated the 187 students as 187 independent personality factors.
They replaced all self-ratings with observations of the students’ parents.
questions.promptZh: 心理学家怎样把人格词汇整理为更宽泛的因子？
optionsZh: 让评分者不经统计分析选出最熟悉的五个词。
收集自我评分，再用因素分析把词汇归组。
把 187 名学生视为 187 个独立人格因子。
把所有自评换成对学生父母的观察。
analyses: A 原文明确用了 factor analysis，非仅凭熟悉度选择。
B rate themselves 后接 applied...factor analysis，顺序与方法均对应。
C 因子是把词语评分归类形成的组，不能把一个参与者人数值当作因子数。
D themselves 表示自评，没有父母观察这一程序。

options: The sequence has reached its final item.
The next item contradicts every earlier example.
Further similar items could be added.
The examples must be repeated in reverse order.

optionsZh: 这一列举已到最后一项。
下一项将反驳之前所有例子。
还可继续列出类似项目。
必须把例子倒过来重复。
analyses: A 省略后续类似项目，不是宣告没有其他项目。
B 不含转折或反驳关系。
C 是“等等、诸如此类”的意思，提示列举未穷尽。
D and so on 表示还可继续列举同类项目，不涉及倒序；这里列出的自评问题只是例子，并非全部1,710项。

questions.passage: “So what?” you might ask (despite reading the last chapter). Aren’t these activities all what the philosopher Blaise Pascal would have called “diversions”? Other than filling people’s time to avoid boredom, do these activities have any genuine benefits? In other words, what is the point of exploration?
questions.prompt: What doubt is raised about exploration?
options: Whether every activity has already been shown to be harmful.
Whether Pascal personally attended all these events.
Whether these experiences offer benefits beyond filling time and avoiding boredom.
Whether people can ever feel bored at all.
questions.promptZh: 这里对探索提出什么疑问？
optionsZh: 每种活动是否已被证明有害。
Pascal 是否亲自参加过这些活动。
这些体验除了打发时间、避免无聊，还有没有益处。
人是否可能无聊。
analyses: A genuine benefits 是追问，不是已证明有害。
B would have called 是作者设想的哲学归类，不是 Pascal 的行程。
C Other than filling...genuine benefits 与 point of exploration 概括质疑。
D avoid boredom 已承认无聊这一可能。设问提出研究动机，不能把怀疑读成作者已宣布全部无益。

questions.passage: When I was in Charlottesville, I would go to a local coffee shop every day and never went to Starbucks. But when I was traveling, I would realize that all of a sudden I loved going to Starbucks. When I was in the psychology building (Gilmer Hall) in Charlottesville and saw a graduate student walking by, I would greet them with a very curt “hey.” When I saw the same graduate student at a conference in Las Vegas, I went “Hey, Gary, so nice to see you!” and almost hugged him.
questions.prompt: How did the author’s responses change when he travelled?
options: He avoided Starbucks both at home and away.
He welcomed familiar stores and people more warmly away from home.
He greeted the student more curtly in Las Vegas.
He visited Starbucks every day in Charlottesville.
questions.promptZh: 旅行时作者的反应怎样变化？
optionsZh: 在家出门都避开 Starbucks。
出门时更热情地欢迎熟悉店铺和熟人。
在 Las Vegas 更冷淡招呼学生。
在 Charlottesville 天天去 Starbucks。
analyses: A traveling 时突然喜欢去，与此相反。
B 咖啡店偏好和对同一学生的招呼都随地点变化。
C curt hey 是校内，旅行见面更热情。
D 在当地去 local coffee shop，never went to Starbucks。这里是个人轶事，不是群体实验结果。

evidence.quote: when I was traveling, I would realize that all of a sudden I loved going to Starbucks.
Hey, Gary, so nice to see you!

vocabulary.context: 描述校园内随意冷淡的 hey，与外地热情招呼形成对比
vocabulary.example: He answered with a curt greeting.

每位旅客总会拥抱熟悉学生。

B 不是当前解释的内容。

questions.passage: The great surprise of resilience research is the ordinariness of the phenomena. Resilience appears to be a common phenomenon that results in most cases from the operation of basic human adaptational systems.”
questions.prompt: What is the surprising conclusion about resilience?
options: It commonly emerges from basic human adaptation rather than rare invincibility.
It is always a property possessed by only one exceptional child.
It guarantees that no survivor feels pain.
It requires falling exactly seven times in a literal test.
questions.promptZh: 关于韧性的惊人结论是什么？
optionsZh: 常来自基本适应系统，而非罕见无敌。
永远只属一名特殊儿童。
保证幸存者无痛。
必须真实测试恰跌七次。
analyses: A ordinariness/common/basic adaptational systems共同支持。
B common与only相反。
C 韧性不是无痛保证。
D 本段讲韧性与基本适应机制，并没有设置或规定跌倒次数的实验。

questions.passage: Research provides empirical evidence for a popular Japanese proverb: “Fall seven times, stand up an eighth time” (七転八起).
questions.prompt: What does the Japanese proverb suggest about responding to repeated setbacks?
options: Recovery depends on having exceptional personal powers.
Further efforts should stop after repeated failures.
Resilience requires avoiding all future setbacks.
Continue getting up after falling repeatedly.
questions.promptZh: 此印刷续片在原段落中起什么作用？
optionsZh: 开始新的COVID结果。
完整新小节标题。
给出韧性数值估计。
结束上一短段开始的括号内日语谚语。
analyses: A 谚语讲反复跌倒后再站起，并未把恢复能力归因于少数人的特殊天赋。
B stand up an eighth time 与停止尝试的说法相反。
C 原文保留了 fall 的情境，并没有要求或保证避免所有挫折。
D 跌倒后再次站起，支持面对反复挫折仍继续尝试的有限推断；谚语并非要求字面跌倒七次的实验程序，也不保证任何人的恢复结果。

questions.passage: For a well-educated and well-traveled person, Peter is truly clueless as to what he wants in his life. When he was young, he thought he would be a writer. Sally asked, “Have you written?” Peter replied, at age fifty-two, “Not a word!” and laughed.
questions.prompt: What discrepancy about Peter is emphasized?
options: He lacked any education but published several novels.
He had fulfilled every youthful ambition before fifty-two.
He never expressed any interest in becoming a writer.
Despite education, travel, and a youthful writing ambition, he says he has written nothing.
optionsZh: 无教育却出版多部小说。
52岁前实现所有青年抱负。
从未想过当作家。
受过教育、旅行多、年轻想写作，却说一字未写。
analyses: A well-educated与缺乏教育相反；Not a word也不支持已出版。
B truly clueless及未写字与全部实现相反。

D 资历、抱负与实际自述之间的反差明确；这是对小说人物的讨论，不是说本书作者未写过字。

evidence.quote: When he was young, he thought he would be a writer.

His attachment to Clarissa persists despite another love in India.
He remembers Clarissa only as a stranger at the party.

analyses: A Throughout the novel...thinks about明显不是抹去。

Comparing exactly twelve countries on every trip.
Exploring at least twelve possibilities before selecting one.
Keeping twelve apartments at the same time.
